verdictStatement: This is a ledger-only generation and it does the ledger work correctly. The frozen Codex v12 REJECT is now pinned at bcd92ff7…, which matches both the dispatch and my own measurement, and its entry lists all three findings — CPCV12-B1, S1 and S2 — against a verdict I parsed independently as 1 blocker, 2 SHOULD-FIX, 0 advisories. The disposition of B1 is accurate rather than convenient: I read B1 in the frozen verdict and its own scope field says dispatch-integrity and its locations are the v12 review-prompt file, not the subject, so v14's 'no subject-byte repair. Do not retarget v12' is the right call and not an evasion. The two already-folded claims are verifiable and verified at v13's bytes rather than taken on trust: mapKeyCount is 80 against exactly 80 members at v13 and still at v14, and /date is genuinely on v13's closed roster. The dispatched mapKeyCount attack therefore fails at both generations, with archiveGoldenKeyCount 17 and acceptanceTestKeyCount 10 also matching their actual member counts. Nothing substantive moved: conformanceReport, archiveProfile, acceptanceTests, fixtureGeneration, recordedInputs and seven more blocks are byte-identical to v13, so the roster's 'No fixtureMemberMap, archive, or COORD pin change' is true by measurement. My own v13 advisory is booked as carried rather than quietly dropped. The single advisory is that the ledger rotation lost two records on the way in.

I searched the whole of v14 for the subject digest and it appears nowhere.
instanceOne.mitigation: The not-retargeted instruction survives in prose at honestyRepairsFromV13[0] ('Do not retarget v12'), and provenance remains recoverable one hop away because each generation pins its immediate predecessor — v14 pins v13 at 234831d9…, and v13 pins v12. There is also a coherent reading in which this is normalisation rather than loss: appliesFindingsOf is a findings ledger, and after v14 it contains only verdict entries. But under that reading the subject pin should have moved somewhere rather than vanished.

instanceTwo.what: The codexv10 entry lost its advisories key. v13 recorded it as blockers [CPCV10-B1], shouldFix [CPCV10-S1, CPCV10-S2], advisories []. v14 keeps everything but drops the empty advisories array, while the two entries added in the same object — codexv12 and claude2v13 — both carry advisories. instanceTwo.mitigation: Nothing false is stated and no finding is lost; omitting an empty array does not assert that Codex v10 had advisories.

advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: Neither instance states anything false, neither touches the contract's substance, and the v12 provenance is recoverable through the predecessor chain. I record them together because they are one pattern — records shed during ledger rotation — and because that pattern is the subject of my own v13 advisory ADV-V13-01, which v14 explicitly books as not folded. The artifact is aware of the class and chose to carry it; performing two more instances of it while doing so is worth the coordinator seeing, but it does not meet the bar I have applied elsewhere for a SHOULD-FIX, which is a statement false as written or a refuted closure claim.
advisories.suggestedFix: Restore advisories: [] on codexv10 so all three entries share one shape, and either keep a subject-pin block or state once that subject provenance is carried by the basedOn chain rather than by this ledger.

coordinatorNote: A narrow, well-executed ledger generation. The part worth the coordinator's attention is that the two 'already folded at v13' claims are the kind that are easy to accept and I did not: both are checkable in v13's own bytes and both hold, and the B1 disposition is likewise verified against B1's own text rather than against v14's summary of it. One scope limit applies to this ACCEPT: the Codex v13 verdict is not on my read list, so I did not read it or pin it, and I do not certify v14's account of CODEX-V13-S1 against that text — I verified the repair's substance from the frozen Codex v12 instead. v14 books that same exposure itself. The single advisory is that the rotation shed two records on the way in — the v12 subject pin entirely, and one predecessor entry's empty advisories field — which is the same pattern as my carried v13 advisory. Nothing false, nothing substantive, and provenance is recoverable through the predecessor chain, so it does not withhold acceptance. DR-120 remains OPEN, no packager or toolchain is chosen, and nothing here marks DR-120 or DR-103 SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
